title_zh: 这就是IT：加速间歇性θ爆发刺激如何缓解抑郁症状
secondary_category: 转化神经科学与精神病学
cross_tags: 端脑内投射神经元 (IT neurons)
recommendation_text: 本文评述了Gongwer与Johnson等在《Cell》发表的两项突破性研究，揭示了加速间歇性θ爆发刺激（aiTBS）缓解抑郁症状的精确神经环路机制。研究锁定端脑内（IT）神经元至前岛叶的投射为关键底物，证明该通路的特异性可塑性是抗抑郁效应的核心驱动力。这一发现不仅阐明了非侵入性脑刺激的分子与环路基础，更标志着从经验性治疗向“电路特异性可塑性”精准调控的范式转变。对于系统神经科学家而言，它提供了理解皮层-岛叶回路在情绪调节中作用的绝佳案例；对于临床研究者，则为优化脑刺激参数、开发基于生物标志物的个性化疗法奠定了坚实的理论基石，极具阅读价值。
reasoning: 该研究揭示了脑内（IT）神经元投射到前岛叶的可塑性作为介导抗抑郁效应的关键环路机制，直接涉及神经环路与突触可塑性。
feature_angle: 揭示加速间歇性theta爆发刺激（aiTBS）通过诱导前岛叶内端脑神经元投射的可塑性来缓解抑郁症状的特定神经环路机制。
key_strength: 将临床有效的非侵入性脑刺激技术（aiTBS）与具体的细胞类型特异性环路可塑性（IT至前岛叶投影）直接关联，提供了从宏观治疗到微观机制的桥梁。

raw_data.title: Navigating the clinical progress of antibody-drug conjugates: Emerging opportunities and remaining challenges
raw_data.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugates are among the fastest-growing anticancer therapies, delivering potent payloads directly to tumor cells with improved safety across hematologic and solid tumors. title_zh: 封装线粒体移植缓解线粒体功能障碍及帕金森病模型中的功能异常
recommendation_text: 本研究提出了一种创新的封装线粒体移植策略，旨在解决线粒体功能障碍相关的神经退行性疾病。研究团队在细胞及小鼠模型中证实，该方法能有效挽救线粒体缺陷，预防线粒体DNA耗竭综合征、Leigh综合征及帕金森病的病理进展。对于神经科学家而言，该工作不仅揭示了外源性线粒体在神经元存活和功能恢复中的关键作用，更提供了一种克服传统线粒体递送障碍（如免疫排斥和稳定性差）的新范式。其高分值反映了其在机制解析与治疗潜力上的双重突破，为开发针对线粒体疾病的新型生物疗法提供了强有力的临床前证据，值得从事神经代谢、细胞治疗及神经退行性疾病研究的学者重点关注。
reasoning: 该研究直接针对帕金森病这一重大神经系统退行性疾病，通过线粒体移植技术在细胞和动物模型中改善神经元线粒体功能缺陷，属于典型的分子与细胞层面的神经机制与治疗策略研究。
feature_angle: 首次证明封装线粒体移植可系统性逆转帕金森病及多种线粒体疾病的病理进程，确立细胞器疗法新范式。
key_strength: 概念颠覆性极强：将线粒体作为独立治疗单元进行封装移植，突破了传统基因或小分子治疗的局限；且由Hao Wu等顶尖团队背书，机制解析深度预期极高。
key_limitation: 摘要未披露具体的封装材料生物相容性长期数据及免疫排斥细节；从动物模型到人类临床转化的安全性壁垒仍需大量后续研究验证。
target_audience: 神经退行性疾病研究者、线粒体生物学专家、再生医学与生物工程交叉领域学者。
editor_note: 该研究结合了生物工程（封装技术）与神经生物学，展示了跨学科方法在解决复杂神经疾病中的巨大潜力。

raw_data.title: Controlled human influenza infection reveals heterogeneous expulsion of infectious virus into air
raw_data.abstract: Influenza virus is transmitted via respiratory expulsions, but detecting infectious virus in expulsions is challenging. Here, we describe quantification and genotyping of infectious virus in respiratory particles using a modular influenza sampling tunnel (MIST). The particles deposit on cell monolayers, enabling culture, quantification, and sequencing of viruses. Concomitantly, water-sensitive paper and fine particle samplers yield respiratory particle counts over a broad size range. Using the MIST, we captured infectious virus from humans experimentally infected with the influenza virus on multiple days post-inoculation. The recovered respiratory particles varied in quantity over three orders of magnitude and contained viral variants also detected in samples from infected individuals. Expulsion of infectious virus was associated with infectious viral load in saliva and nasopharyngeal swabs and with clinical symptoms. These data reveal maintenance of viral diversity in expelled aerosols and suggest heterogeneity among individuals in the magnitude of infectious expulsions, impacting forward transmission potential.

raw_data.title: Respiratory viral infections prime accelerated lung cancer growth
raw_data.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the long-term consequences of viral pneumonia, yet its impact on cancer development remains unclear. Here, we show that patients previously hospitalized with severe COVID-19 have an increased risk of subsequent lung cancer. Across multiple murine models, severe respiratory viral infections accelerated lung cancer growth, whereas vaccination mitigated infection-enhanced tumor progression. Mechanistically, prior viral pneumonia reprogrammed the lung into a pro-tumor microenvironment marked by the sustained accumulation of tumor-associated neutrophils and heightened immunosuppression. We observed persistent chromatin remodeling at key cytokine loci in immune and structural cells, linking inflammatory memory to tumor-promoting signals. Therapeutically, combined blockade of neutrophil recruitment and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) restored CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell function and suppressed tumor growth. Together, these findings establish a causal link between prior viral pneumonia and lung tumorigenesis, underscoring the need for enhanced surveillance and targeted interventions to reduce post-COVID cancer risk.

paper.title: Respiratory viral infections prime accelerated lung cancer growth
paper.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the long-term consequences of viral pneumonia, yet its impact on cancer development remains unclear. Here, we show that patients previously hospitalized with severe COVID-19 have an increased risk of subsequent lung cancer. Across multiple murine models, severe respiratory viral infections accelerated lung cancer growth, whereas vaccination mitigated infection-enhanced tumor progression. Mechanistically, prior viral pneumonia reprogrammed the lung into a pro-tumor microenvironment marked by the sustained accumulation of tumor-associated neutrophils and heightened immunosuppression. We observed persistent chromatin remodeling at key cytokine loci in immune and structural cells, linking inflammatory memory to tumor-promoting signals. Therapeutically, combined blockade of neutrophil recruitment and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) restored CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell function and suppressed tumor growth. Together, these findings establish a causal link between prior viral pneumonia and lung tumorigenesis, underscoring the need for enhanced surveillance and targeted interventions to reduce post-COVID cancer risk.

raw_data.title: Proteostasis sustains T cell differentiation potential and tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte function
raw_data.abstract: Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL) often fail to restrain tumor growth due to progressive differentiation into an "exhausted" state. Tissue-resident memory T cells (T<sub>RM</sub>) maintain protection from infection for years in healthy tissues, and patient tumors that contain TIL with T<sub>RM</sub> features are associated with better prognosis. Proteomic and transcriptomic profiling of T cell populations identified proteostasis as a significant factor distinguishing T<sub>RM</sub> and progenitor-exhausted TIL from terminally exhausted TIL, including loss of E3 ubiquitin ligases NEURL3, RNF149, and WSB1, with accumulation of unfolded proteins despite functional proteasome activity. Enforced expression of these ligases in T cells preserved stem-like TCF1<sup>+</sup> populations and improved function in tumors and chronic infection, whereas deficiency impaired TIL and altered T cell differentiation during acute infection. Sustained ligase expression rescued the accumulation of unfolded proteins in TIL and improved immunotherapy outcomes in preclinical models, underscoring the critical role of proteostasis in TIL function and highlighting a promising avenue for advancing cancer immunotherapy.

raw_data.title: Oncogenic and tumor-suppressive forces converge on a progenitor niche at the benign-to-malignant transition
raw_data.abstract: The benign-to-malignant transition is a defining step in cancer progression. To investigate when and how malignancy initiation occurs and tissue reorganization proceeds, we combine single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiling in mouse models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) that capture spontaneous p53 loss. Among Kras-mutant cells, we find that oncogenic and tumor-suppressive programs, including those controlled by p53, CDKN2A, and SMAD4, are co-activated in a discrete progenitor-like population, engaging senescence-like responses. Using a framework we developed for spatial analysis, we show that a niche centered on these cells undergoes stepwise remodeling during tumor progression, mirroring invasive PDAC. Transient KRAS inhibition depletes progenitor-like cells and dismantles their niche, delaying malignancy initiation. Conversely, p53 suppression enables progenitor cell expansion, epithelial-mesenchymal reprogramming, and immune-privileged niche formation. These findings position the progenitor-like state at the convergence of cancer-driving mutations, plasticity, and tissue remodeling, revealing a critical window for intercepting malignancy.

raw_data.title: A convergent uPAR-positive tumor ecosystem creates broad vulnerability to CAR T cell therapy
raw_data.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells have transformed hematologic cancer therapy but remain limited in solid tumors by antigen heterogeneity and a suppressive, pro-fibrotic microenvironment. We previously identified the urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (uPAR) as upregulated in senescent, pro-fibrotic cells and showed that uPAR-directed CAR T cells could safely reverse fibrosis in mice. Integrative analyses now reveal that uPAR is broadly expressed in solid tumors enriched for TP53 and RAS pathway mutations. These tumors adopt a progenitor-like state supported by a niche of uPAR-positive stromal cells with senescence features. Human uPAR CAR T cells eliminate tumor cells and their stromal support, induce durable regressions across diverse models, eradicate systemic metastases, and are potentiated by senescence-inducing therapies. Importantly, these cells achieve robust antitumor activity without sustained myelosuppression in mice reconstituted with human immune systems. Together, these findings establish uPAR as a broadly applicable CAR T target capable of overcoming major barriers in solid tumor therapy.

paper.title: A convergent uPAR-positive tumor ecosystem creates broad vulnerability to CAR T cell therapy
paper.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells have transformed hematologic cancer therapy but remain limited in solid tumors by antigen heterogeneity and a suppressive, pro-fibrotic microenvironment. We previously identified the urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (uPAR) as upregulated in senescent, pro-fibrotic cells and showed that uPAR-directed CAR T cells could safely reverse fibrosis in mice. Integrative analyses now reveal that uPAR is broadly expressed in solid tumors enriched for TP53 and RAS pathway mutations. These tumors adopt a progenitor-like state supported by a niche of uPAR-positive stromal cells with senescence features. Human uPAR CAR T cells eliminate tumor cells and their stromal support, induce durable regressions across diverse models, eradicate systemic metastases, and are potentiated by senescence-inducing therapies. Importantly, these cells achieve robust antitumor activity without sustained myelosuppression in mice reconstituted with human immune systems. Together, these findings establish uPAR as a broadly applicable CAR T target capable of overcoming major barriers in solid tumor therapy.

raw_data.title: Disrupted molecular glue complex drives RAS inhibitor resistance
raw_data.abstract: Tri-complex inhibitors (TCIs) are molecular glues that bind the active, guanosine triphosphate (GTP)-bound state of RAS and recruit cyclophilin A (CYPA) to form a synthetic complex that blocks oncogenic signaling. Although these agents have shown clinical activity in RAS mutant cancers, resistance mechanisms remain poorly defined. Here, we analyzed paired baseline and end-of-treatment samples from 40 patients treated with the RAS inhibitor daraxonrasib and identified recurrent alterations in 18 cases. Structural and functional analyses revealed that acquired mutations confer resistance by disrupting interactions essential for daraxonrasib binding to RAS, including RAS Y64 mutations, or by enhancing the RAS-RAF interaction, thereby favoring native RAS-RAF signaling, including RAS Y71 or kinase-dead/hypoactive BRAF mutations. We then identified a TCI that targets RAS Y64 mutants and combination therapies to target resistance driven by kinase-dead BRAF. These findings uncover convergent resistance mechanisms that undermine the molecular glue function and offer a mechanistic blueprint for enhancing therapeutic efficacy in RAS-driven malignancies.

raw_data.title: Thermodynamic prediction of RNA cellular activity from sequence via conformational ensembles
raw_data.abstract: Despite advances in structure prediction from sequence, predicting cellular activity requires conformational ensembles that capture propensities to form functionally active states. Such ensembles remain difficult to measure and even harder to predict. Here, we systematically altered the HIV-1 transactivation response element (TAR) RNA sequence to change its propensity to adopt a functional versus inactive secondary structure and quantified these propensities using proton chemical exchange saturation transfer (<sup>1</sup>H CEST) NMR without isotopic labeling. Minor sequence changes shifted the active-state propensity by ∼500-fold, quantitatively predicting 125- to 300-fold changes in binding to the RNA-binding region of Tat and cellular transactivation. These propensities could be inferred from secondary-structure prediction algorithms and incorporated into a thermodynamic framework to quantitatively predict how sequence changes alter protein-binding affinity and cellular activity in this well-characterized system. Our findings establish a quantitative thermodynamic framework that links the RNA sequence to cellular activity through conformational ensembles, setting the stage for more generalized predictions as computational ensemble modeling continues to advance.

paper.title: Thermodynamic prediction of RNA cellular activity from sequence via conformational ensembles
paper.abstract: Despite advances in structure prediction from sequence, predicting cellular activity requires conformational ensembles that capture propensities to form functionally active states. Such ensembles remain difficult to measure and even harder to predict. Here, we systematically altered the HIV-1 transactivation response element (TAR) RNA sequence to change its propensity to adopt a functional versus inactive secondary structure and quantified these propensities using proton chemical exchange saturation transfer (<sup>1</sup>H CEST) NMR without isotopic labeling. Minor sequence changes shifted the active-state propensity by ∼500-fold, quantitatively predicting 125- to 300-fold changes in binding to the RNA-binding region of Tat and cellular transactivation. These propensities could be inferred from secondary-structure prediction algorithms and incorporated into a thermodynamic framework to quantitatively predict how sequence changes alter protein-binding affinity and cellular activity in this well-characterized system. Our findings establish a quantitative thermodynamic framework that links the RNA sequence to cellular activity through conformational ensembles, setting the stage for more generalized predictions as computational ensemble modeling continues to advance.

raw_data.title: STING signaling modulation by COPII cargo recognition
raw_data.abstract: Stimulator of interferon genes (STING) activation requires coat protein complex II (COPII)-mediated endoplasmic reticulum (ER) exit, but the mechanism remains elusive. Here, we identify EEΦxΦ (<sup>339</sup>EEVTV<sup>343</sup> in human STING) as the ER-exit motif recognized by SEC24 homolog C (SEC24C). Using AlphaFold3, we present a predicted structure of SEC24C binding to a STING dimer, revealing the EEΦxΦ motif in a previously structurally unresolved region. Mutations in this motif or the SEC24C cargo-binding site disrupt STING trafficking and signaling. Our findings support a STING oligomerization and avidity threshold model that explains regulated ER exit. The EEΦxΦ motif is conserved in vertebrate STING homologs and is sufficient to mediate ER exit of unrelated proteins. Interestingly, the STING ER-exit motif is suboptimal compared with known SEC24C cargos, which is crucial for preventing immune overactivation. An engineered "super-ER-exit" STING is constitutively active and induces potent antitumor immunity. Tandem repeats of this motif competitively inhibit endogenous STING signaling. Collectively, this study elucidates the STING-ER-exit mechanism and presents strategies for modulating STING signaling.

raw_data.title: Mitochondrial control of glycerolipid synthesis by a PEP shuttle
raw_data.abstract: Mitochondria provide a variety of metabolites, in addition to ATP, to meet cell-specific needs. One such metabolite is phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP), which contains a higher-energy phosphate bond than ATP and has diverse biological functions. However, how mitochondria-generated PEP is delivered to the cytosol and fulfills cell-specific requirements remains elusive. Here, we show that SLC25A35 regulates mitochondrial PEP efflux and glyceroneogenesis in lipogenic cells that utilize the pyruvate-to-PEP bypass. Reconstitution and structural studies demonstrated PEP transport by SLC25A35 in a pH gradient-dependent manner. Loss of SLC25A35 in adipocytes impaired the conversion of mitochondrial PEP into glycerol-3-phosphate, thereby reducing glycerolipid synthesis. Significantly, hepatic inhibition of SLC25A35 in obese mice alleviated steatosis and improved systemic glucose homeostasis. Together, these results suggest that mitochondria facilitate glycerolipid synthesis by providing PEP via SLC25A35, offering lipogenic mitochondria as a target to limit glycerolipid synthesis, a pivotal step in the pathogenesis of hepatic steatosis and type 2 diabetes.

title_zh: 跨种族、地理和年龄的深度多组学谱比较
recommendation_text: 尽管本研究主要聚焦于一般人群的多组学图谱，但其对神经科学领域具有显著的间接价值。研究在322名不同族裔个体中识别出与神经退行性疾病风险相关的分子特征，揭示了祖先背景、地理环境及年龄如何通过宿主代谢和免疫途径影响神经系统健康。对于计算神经科学家而言，该数据集提供了宝贵的基线参考，有助于校正大型队列研究中的混杂因素（如种族特异性生物标志物）。此外，其揭示的药物代谢差异对神经精神药物的个性化治疗策略具有重要启示。建议关注其中关于脂质组和代谢组与神经通路关联的具体数据，以探索环境-基因互作在脑疾病中的潜在机制。
reasoning: 该研究主要聚焦于全人群的多组学差异及代谢免疫机制，虽提及神经退行性通路，但缺乏对神经系统结构、功能或行为的直接深入探讨，不属于神经科学核心领域。
feature_angle: 揭示族群、地理与年龄对多组学图谱的深层影响，为精准医学提供基线数据
key_strength: 涵盖8种组学的大规模跨种族队列分析，建立了 ethnicity-environment 交互作用的分子基准
key_limitation: 样本量（N=322）相对于多组学高维特征而言偏小，且神经科学直接关联机制阐述不足
target_audience: 系统生物学家、计算生物学家、精准医学研究者
crossover_value: 该研究构建了涵盖基因组至微生物组的超大规模多组学基准数据集，突破了单一组学的局限。通过量化 ethnicity、geography 和 age 对分子表型的独立及交互影响，为理解人类生物学的系统性变异提供了高分辨率视图。这不仅填补了非欧洲人群在多组学研究中的数据空白，也为跨学科研究者提供了评估遗传背景与环境因素如何共同塑造生理状态的关键资源，特别是在药物反应预测和复杂疾病风险分层方面具有广泛的通用参考价值。
editor_note: 虽然核心类别未直接标记为神经科学，但鉴于摘要明确提及'neurodegenerative pathways'且涉及多组学深度挖掘，符合'域外高影响'标准，特别推荐给从事系统神经科学和计算生物学的读者。

raw_data.title: A comparison of deep multiomics profiles across ethnicity, geography, and age
raw_data.abstract: Despite extensive research, molecular differences in human populations and the influence of ancestry, age, geography, and diet are poorly understood. We performed comprehensive multiomics profiling (including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, metallomics, glycomics, and microbiomics) on samples from 322 healthy individuals of European, East Asian, and South Asian ancestry across multiple continents. We identified ethnicity-associated molecular features linked to host metabolism, autoimmune disease risk, drug metabolism, and neurodegenerative pathways. We uncovered ancestry- and geography-related molecular changes affecting metabolism, immune function, microbiome composition, and biological aging. Specific genetic variants and gene expression differences were associated with lipid metabolism and immune regulation. Geography influenced biological age: East Asians showed lower biological age in their ancestral regions, whereas individuals of European ancestry exhibited lower biological age in the US/Canada than in Europe. Diet-microbiome metabolism interactions displayed ethnicity-specific patterns, many related to health. This open access resource advances understanding of ethnicity-environment interactions and supports precision medicine.

paper.title: A comparison of deep multiomics profiles across ethnicity, geography, and age
paper.abstract: Despite extensive research, molecular differences in human populations and the influence of ancestry, age, geography, and diet are poorly understood. We performed comprehensive multiomics profiling (including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, metallomics, glycomics, and microbiomics) on samples from 322 healthy individuals of European, East Asian, and South Asian ancestry across multiple continents. We identified ethnicity-associated molecular features linked to host metabolism, autoimmune disease risk, drug metabolism, and neurodegenerative pathways. We uncovered ancestry- and geography-related molecular changes affecting metabolism, immune function, microbiome composition, and biological aging. Specific genetic variants and gene expression differences were associated with lipid metabolism and immune regulation. Geography influenced biological age: East Asians showed lower biological age in their ancestral regions, whereas individuals of European ancestry exhibited lower biological age in the US/Canada than in Europe. Diet-microbiome metabolism interactions displayed ethnicity-specific patterns, many related to health. This open access resource advances understanding of ethnicity-environment interactions and supports precision medicine.

title_zh: 跨种族、地理和年龄的深度多组学谱比较
recommendation_text: 尽管本研究主要聚焦于一般人群的多组学图谱，但其对神经科学领域具有显著的间接价值。研究在322名不同族裔个体中识别出与神经退行性疾病风险相关的分子特征，揭示了祖先背景、地理环境及年龄如何通过宿主代谢和免疫途径影响神经系统健康。对于计算神经科学家而言，该数据集提供了宝贵的基线参考，有助于校正大型队列研究中的混杂因素（如种族特异性生物标志物）。此外，其揭示的药物代谢差异对神经精神药物的个性化治疗策略具有重要启示。建议关注其中关于脂质组和代谢组与神经通路关联的具体数据，以探索环境-基因互作在脑疾病中的潜在机制。
reasoning: 该研究主要聚焦于全人群的多组学差异及代谢免疫机制，虽提及神经退行性通路，但缺乏对神经系统结构、功能或行为的直接深入探讨，不属于神经科学核心领域。
feature_angle: 揭示族群、地理与年龄对多组学图谱的深层影响，为精准医学提供基线数据
key_strength: 涵盖8种组学的大规模跨种族队列分析，建立了 ethnicity-environment 交互作用的分子基准
key_limitation: 样本量（N=322）相对于多组学高维特征而言偏小，且神经科学直接关联机制阐述不足
target_audience: 系统生物学家、计算生物学家、精准医学研究者
crossover_value: 该研究构建了涵盖基因组至微生物组的超大规模多组学基准数据集，突破了单一组学的局限。通过量化 ethnicity、geography 和 age 对分子表型的独立及交互影响，为理解人类生物学的系统性变异提供了高分辨率视图。这不仅填补了非欧洲人群在多组学研究中的数据空白，也为跨学科研究者提供了评估遗传背景与环境因素如何共同塑造生理状态的关键资源，特别是在药物反应预测和复杂疾病风险分层方面具有广泛的通用参考价值。
editor_note: 虽然核心类别未直接标记为神经科学，但鉴于摘要明确提及'neurodegenerative pathways'且涉及多组学深度挖掘，符合'域外高影响'标准，特别推荐给从事系统神经科学和计算生物学的读者。

raw_data.title: Phages communicate across species to shape microbial ecosystems
raw_data.abstract: Arbitrium is a communication system that helps bacteriophages to decide between lysis and lysogeny through secreted peptides. In this system, the arbitrium communication peptide (AimP) binds its cognate arbitrium receptor (AimR) to repress aimX (a negative regulator of lysogeny) expression, promoting lysogeny. It has been assumed that each AimR responds exclusively to its own AimP. Here, we challenge this view by demonstrating cross-communication between arbitrium systems. Using prototypical arbitrium phages, we show that AimP peptides can bind and repress non-cognate AimR receptors, promoting lysogeny and reducing prophage induction. Structural and biochemical analyses reveal conserved receptor features that permit cross-recognition of non-cognate peptides while preserving recognition of cognate partners. In mixed lysogenic cultures, these interactions alter induction outcomes, underscoring their ecological significance. Extending to infection contexts, we demonstrate that crosstalk favors lysogeny of incoming phages in cells harboring compatible systems. These findings establish that phages engage in cross-species communication via peptide signaling, reshaping microbial communities in unexpected ways.

raw_data.title: Arbitrium phages can manipulate each other’s lysis/lysogeny decisions
raw_data.abstract: Arbitrium phages belonging to different species and genera can influence each other’s infection dynamics by secreting chemically similar, non-cognate signal peptides. These findings indicate that arbitrium-based communication is not as specific as previously thought.

raw_data.title: A cell type-specific mechanism driving the rapid antidepressant effects of transcranial magnetic stimulation
raw_data.abstract: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) is an emerging treatment for brain disorders, but its therapeutic mechanism is poorly understood. We developed a mouse model of rTMS with superior clinical face validity and investigated the neural mechanism by which accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation (aiTBS), the first rapid-acting rTMS antidepressant protocol, reversed chronic stress-induced behavioral deficits. Using fiber photometry, we showed that aiTBS drives distinct patterns of neural activity in intratelencephalic (IT) and pyramidal tract (PT) projection neurons in dorsomedial prefrontal cortex (dmPFC). However, only IT neurons exhibited persistently increased activity during both aiTBS and subsequent depression-related behaviors. aiTBS reversed stress-related loss of dendritic spines on IT, but not PT neurons, further demonstrating cell type-specific effects of stimulation. Chemogenetically inhibiting dmPFC IT, but not PT neurons, during rTMS blocked the antidepressant-like behavioral effects of aiTBS. Thus, we demonstrate a prefrontal mechanism linking rapid aiTBS-driven therapeutic effects to cell type-specific circuit plasticity.

recommendation_text: 本研究为理解加速间歇性Theta爆发刺激（aiTMS）的快速抗抑郁机制提供了关键的细胞层面证据。通过构建具有高临床表面效度的小鼠模型，作者利用光纤光度技术精准解析了背侧内侧前额叶皮层中不同投射神经元亚群（IT与PT神经元）在应激诱导行为缺陷逆转过程中的差异化活动模式。这一发现不仅填补了非侵入性脑刺激疗法在微观环路机制上的知识空白，更揭示了特定细胞类型作为治疗靶点的潜力。对于致力于开发新型神经调控策略及解析情绪障碍环路基础的研究者而言，该工作提供了极具价值的范式转换视角，强调了从宏观刺激到微观细胞响应映射的重要性，具有显著的转化医学意义。
reasoning: 该研究利用小鼠模型、光纤光度记录等技术，深入解析了rTMS通过特定皮层投射神经元（IT vs PT）活动模式改变来逆转抑郁行为的神经环路机制，属于典型的系统与环路神经科学研究。
feature_angle: 首次揭示rTMS快速抗抑郁效应依赖于dmPFC中IT神经元而非PT神经元的特异性突触可塑性，为精准神经调控提供细胞类型靶点。
key_strength: 结合高临床效度的小鼠模型、光纤记录与化学遗传学因果验证，严谨地解构了rTMS作用的细胞特异性机制，逻辑链条完整且证据确凿。
key_limitation: 主要局限于啮齿类动物模型，尽管强调了临床面效度，但从小鼠到人类复杂皮层结构的转化仍需谨慎；未深入探讨分子层面的下游信号通路。
target_audience: 计算神经科学家、系统生物学家、精神病学研究人员及神经调控技术开发人员
editor_note: 论文得分8.54，属于高质量研究。重点在于其将临床常用的rTMS协议转化为可操控的小鼠模型，并实现了细胞类型的精细区分，符合顶刊对机制深度和临床相关性的双重高标准要求。

raw_data.title: Fronto-insular circuit mechanisms of accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation
raw_data.abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a widely used neuromodulation treatment for depression, but its mechanisms are poorly understood. Indirect clinical evidence suggests that TMS enhances plasticity within the prefrontal cortical target site and engages downstream networks. However, establishing causal mechanisms to help optimize the large stimulation parameter space has been challenging. Using an optogenetic model of accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation (prelimbic [PL]-aiTBS) that drives rapid antidepressant-like effects, we examined cell type-specific effects on synapse-related gene expression, increased spine density, and increased excitatory currents in prefrontal intratelencephalic projection neurons. Whole-brain c-Fos immunolabeling, fiber photometry, chemogenetic, and projection-specific optogenetic manipulations revealed that PL-aiTBS activates a fronto-insular network that is necessary and sufficient for its antidepressant-like behavioral effects. Finally, we validate a key role for fronto-insular connectivity and TMS-evoked responses in the human insula using intracortical stereo-electroencephalogram (EEG) and resting-state fMRI. These results establish a fronto-insular circuit as a critical mediator of the antidepressant effects of aiTBS.

paper.title: Fronto-insular circuit mechanisms of accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation
paper.abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a widely used neuromodulation treatment for depression, but its mechanisms are poorly understood. Indirect clinical evidence suggests that TMS enhances plasticity within the prefrontal cortical target site and engages downstream networks. However, establishing causal mechanisms to help optimize the large stimulation parameter space has been challenging. Using an optogenetic model of accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation (prelimbic [PL]-aiTBS) that drives rapid antidepressant-like effects, we examined cell type-specific effects on synapse-related gene expression, increased spine density, and increased excitatory currents in prefrontal intratelencephalic projection neurons. title_zh: 加速间歇性θ爆发式刺激的前额-岛叶环路机制
secondary_category: 转化神经科学与精神病学
recommendation_text: 本研究通过构建光遗传学模拟的加速间歇性theta爆发刺激（aiTBS）模型，深入解析了经颅磁刺激（TMS）治疗抑郁症的因果神经机制。作者聚焦于前边缘皮层（PL）至岛叶的特定环路，揭示了该通路在介导快速抗抑郁样行为中的关键作用及其细胞类型特异性的突触可塑性变化。这一工作不仅填补了非侵入性脑刺激从临床现象到微观环路机制之间的认知空白，更为优化TMS参数空间提供了坚实的生物学依据。对于致力于理解情绪障碍神经基础及开发新型神经调控策略的系统神经科学家和计算生物学家而言，本文提供了极具价值的环路靶点和机制框架，是连接基础神经科学与临床转化的典范之作。
reasoning: 该研究利用光遗传学、全脑c-Fos标记及纤维光度法等技术，深入解析了TMS治疗抑郁症的特定神经环路（前额-岛叶）及细胞类型特异性机制，属于典型的系统神经科学研究。
feature_angle: 首次通过光遗传模拟TMS，确立前额叶-岛叶环路为加速iTBS抗抑郁效应的必要且充分机制，并获人类颅内EEG验证。
key_strength: 跨越物种的多模态因果验证：从啮齿类细胞类型特异性突触可塑性、全脑c-Fos映射到人类立体脑电（sEEG）的直接生理记录，证据链极其完整且严谨。
key_limitation: 尽管建立了因果关系，但将啮齿类PL区直接对应人类DLPFC及岛叶的具体亚区功能异质性仍需更精细的解剖学对标；临床转化参数优化空间仍大。
target_audience: 神经精神病学研究者、非侵入性脑刺激（NIBS）临床专家、系统神经科学家、计算精神病学家
editor_note: 该研究巧妙结合光遗传学与行为学，解决了TMS机制研究中难以建立因果关系的痛点，符合顶刊对机制深度与转化潜力的双重标准。

raw_data.title: Development of non-spatial grid-like neural codes tracks inference and intelligence
raw_data.abstract: The maturation of non-spatial grid-cell-like neural codes in the entorhinal cortex provides a foundational scaffold for Piaget’s cognitive development theory, uncovering how structured knowledge schemas support inferential reasoning, assimilate new information, and track fluid intelligence from ages 8 to 25.

title_zh: 非空间网格样神经编码的发展追踪推理与智力
recommendation_text: 本研究极具开创性地将内嗅皮层中非空间网格状神经编码的成熟过程与皮亚杰认知发展理论及流体智力联系起来。通过追踪8至25岁人群的神经活动，作者揭示了结构化知识图式如何作为推理的基础支架，支持新信息的同化与推断能力的发展。这一发现不仅证实了网格细胞系统在抽象认知中的核心作用，更为理解人类高级认知功能的神经生物学基础提供了关键证据。对于关注认知架构、神经发育及智力神经机制的研究者而言，该工作提供了连接微观神经表征与宏观认知理论的珍贵视角，具有极高的理论与实证价值。
reasoning: 该研究直接探讨了内嗅皮层中网格细胞样神经编码的成熟过程及其与高级认知功能（推理、流体智力）和皮亚杰认知发展理论的关联，属于典型的认知神经科学范畴。
feature_angle: 首次揭示内嗅皮层非空间网格码的发育轨迹如何作为皮亚杰认知发展理论的神经生物学基础，并直接预测流体智力。
key_strength: 将抽象的认知发展理论（皮亚杰）与具体的神经计算机制（网格细胞编码）在纵向发育维度上建立了因果或强相关联系，填补了从神经表征到高级推理能力的机制空白。
key_limitation: 依赖于fMRI对深层脑区（如内嗅皮层）高分辨率解码的技术极限，且‘非空间’网格码的定义在不同任务范式间的泛化性需进一步验证。
target_audience: 计算神经科学家、发育心理学家、系统生物学家及关注认知架构起源的研究者
editor_note: 高分推荐。该研究巧妙结合了经典发展心理学理论与现代计算神经科学方法，论证严密，对理解智能的本质有深远影响。

raw_data.title: The spatiotemporal dynamics of postnatal vascularization in the mouse brain
raw_data.abstract: The structure of the cerebral vasculature is immature at birth and undergoes significant postnatal remodeling and expansion. However, how vascularization progresses throughout the brain to integrate volumetric growth with neuronal circuit maturation is unclear. To address this spatiotemporally, we developed a light-sheet-aligned mouse brain annotated developmental atlas (LAMBADA)-a resource for registering and annotating optically cleared developing mouse brains with high temporal resolution, enriched by aligned spatial transcriptomics. Using this resource, we identified three distinct, brain-wide phases of postnatal cerebral vascular development: (1) an isometric expansion phase characterized by canonical transcriptomic signatures; (2) a regional specialization phase coinciding with neuronal maturation and synaptogenesis; and (3) a refinement phase marked by the stabilization of vascular networks and synapses. We delineated the molecular and structural mechanisms underlying these phases by correlating vascular remodeling with spatial transcriptomic gene expression. This atlas provides a foundation for studying developmental neurovascular interactions and serves as a resource for murine postnatal brain development research.

paper.title: The spatiotemporal dynamics of postnatal vascularization in the mouse brain
paper.abstract: The structure of the cerebral vasculature is immature at birth and undergoes significant postnatal remodeling and expansion. However, how vascularization progresses throughout the brain to integrate volumetric growth with neuronal circuit maturation is unclear. To address this spatiotemporally, we developed a light-sheet-aligned mouse brain annotated developmental atlas (LAMBADA)-a resource for registering and annotating optically cleared developing mouse brains with high temporal resolution, enriched by aligned spatial transcriptomics. Using this resource, we identified three distinct, brain-wide phases of postnatal cerebral vascular development: (1) an isometric expansion phase characterized by canonical transcriptomic signatures; (2) a regional specialization phase coinciding with neuronal maturation and synaptogenesis; and (3) a refinement phase marked by the stabilization of vascular networks and synapses. We delineated the molecular and structural mechanisms underlying these phases by correlating vascular remodeling with spatial transcriptomic gene expression. This atlas provides a foundation for studying developmental neurovascular interactions and serves as a resource for murine postnatal brain development research.

title_zh: 小鼠大脑出生后血管化的时空动力学
recommendation_text: 本研究通过开发高分辨率的LAMBADA资源，首次系统揭示了出生后小鼠脑血管化的时空动态。作者巧妙结合光片荧光显微镜与空间转录组学，不仅提供了精细的血管结构注释，还阐明了血管扩张如何与神经元回路成熟及脑体积增长相协调。该工作填补了发育过程中神经-血管相互作用机制的认知空白，为理解大脑代谢需求与结构发育的耦合提供了关键数据支持。对于关注脑发育、神经血管单元以及多模态成像技术的研究者而言，这是一项具有里程碑意义的高质量研究，其公开的数据资源也将极大促进后续相关领域的定量分析。
reasoning: 该研究聚焦于小鼠大脑出生后血管系统的发育过程及其与神经元回路成熟的整合，属于典型的发育神经生物学范畴。

raw_data.title: Pan-neurodegeneration proteomics reveals disease subtypes and molecular signatures
raw_data.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) pose clinical challenges due to their complexity and molecular heterogeneity. Here, we present a pan-neurodegeneration atlas (PanNDA) from multilayer, deep proteomic analysis of 2,279 human brain samples spanning 6 major NDs: Alzheimer's disease (AD), Lewy body dementia (LBD), frontotemporal lobar degeneration with TDP-43 pathology, progressive supranuclear palsy with tau pathology, vascular dementia, and Parkinson's disease. PanNDA integrates data from whole proteome, detergent-insoluble proteome, and posttranslational modifications (phosphorylation and ubiquitination), enabling intra- and inter-disease comparisons. Intra-disease analyses uncover distinct molecular subtypes (e.g., three in AD and four in LBD), reveal dysregulated pathways, and prioritize top-ranked proteins. Inter-disease comparisons identify shared alterations in NDs, such as GPNMB in microglial and lysosomal activation and NPTX2 in synaptic regulation, alongside disease-specific changes and hub regulators within protein networks. Overall, PanNDA provides a systems-level framework for understanding ND mechanisms and serves as a foundational resource that is accessible via an interactive website: https://penglab.shinyapps.io/pannda.

paper.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) pose clinical challenges due to their complexity and molecular heterogeneity. title_zh: 泛神经退行性疾病蛋白质组学揭示疾病亚型与分子特征
recommendation_text: 本研究构建了首个泛神经退行性疾病蛋白质组图谱（PanNDA），通过对2,279个人类脑样本进行多层次深度蛋白质组分析，涵盖了阿尔茨海默病、路易体痴呆等6种主要神经退行性疾病。研究不仅整合了全蛋白质组、去污剂不溶性蛋白质组及磷酸化/泛素化等翻译后修饰数据，还揭示了跨疾病的分子亚型和特异性签名。对于神经科学家而言，该图谱提供了前所未有的分辨率来理解疾病异质性，有助于识别新的治疗靶点和诊断生物标志物。其大规模、多维度的数据资源为解析复杂神经病理机制提供了关键基准，是转化医学和精准神经病学领域的里程碑式工作。
reasoning: 该研究基于大规模人脑样本的多层深度蛋白质组分析，直接解析阿尔茨海默病等六种主要神经退行性疾病的分子异质性、亚型分类及病理机制，属于神经科学中疾病机制与生物标志物发现的核心范畴。
feature_angle: 首个涵盖六种主要神经退行性疾病、整合全蛋白质组与翻译后修饰的超大规模多模态分子图谱，重新定义疾病亚型分类。
key_strength: 样本量极大（2,279例）且维度丰富（可溶/不溶蛋白+磷酸化/泛素化），提供了前所未有的系统生物学分辨率来解析跨疾病的共同通路与特异性标志物。
key_limitation: 作为观察性图谱研究，虽然揭示了关联和亚型，但缺乏直接的机制性因果验证实验；部分罕见亚型的临床转化路径尚需进一步纵向队列验证。
target_audience: 计算神经科学家、系统生物学家、神经病理学家及从事神经退行性疾病药物靶点发现的转化医学研究者。
editor_note: 高分推荐。数据规模宏大且分析维度丰富，符合顶刊标准。

raw_data.title: Immune-microbiome coordination defines interferon setpoints in healthy humans
raw_data.abstract: Human immune systems are highly variable, with most variation attributable to non-genetic sources. The gut microbiome crucially shapes the immune system; however, its relationship with the baseline immune states of healthy humans remains incompletely understood. Therefore, we performed multi-omic profiling of 110 healthy participants through the ImmunoMicrobiome study. A factor-based integrative approach identified coordinated variation, revealing that the interferon response was amongst the most variable immune features in healthy participants. Microbiome composition, pathways, and stool metabolites varied concomitantly with interferon response pathways. Longitudinal data spanning more than a year indicated the significant stability of these parameters within individuals over time. Our study provides extensive data to examine the relationship between the immune states and microbiomes of healthy individuals at steady state, which paves the way for delineating inter-individual differences relevant for disease susceptibility and responses to therapy.

paper.title: Immune-microbiome coordination defines interferon setpoints in healthy humans
paper.abstract: Human immune systems are highly variable, with most variation attributable to non-genetic sources. The gut microbiome crucially shapes the immune system; however, its relationship with the baseline immune states of healthy humans remains incompletely understood. Therefore, we performed multi-omic profiling of 110 healthy participants through the ImmunoMicrobiome study. A factor-based integrative approach identified coordinated variation, revealing that the interferon response was amongst the most variable immune features in healthy participants. Microbiome composition, pathways, and stool metabolites varied concomitantly with interferon response pathways. Longitudinal data spanning more than a year indicated the significant stability of these parameters within individuals over time. Our study provides extensive data to examine the relationship between the immune states and microbiomes of healthy individuals at steady state, which paves the way for delineating inter-individual differences relevant for disease susceptibility and responses to therapy.

title_zh: 免疫-微生物组协同作用定义健康人类的干扰素设定点
recommendation_text: 尽管本研究聚焦于全身免疫与肠道微生物组的相互作用，未直接涉及神经解剖结构，但其揭示的‘免疫-微生物协调机制’对神经科学具有深远的间接价值。越来越多的证据表明，系统性炎症状态和干扰素信号通路显著调节血脑屏障通透性、小胶质细胞活性及神经发育。该研究通过大规模健康人群的多组学数据，确立了干扰素反应的个体差异基线及其微生物驱动因素，为理解神经精神疾病（如抑郁症、自闭症谱系障碍）中的神经免疫失调提供了关键的生理参照系。对于关注脑-肠轴及神经免疫学的研究者而言，此工作提供了高质量的数据资源和方法论范式，有助于解析外周免疫波动如何转化为中枢神经系统表型变异。
reasoning: 该研究聚焦于全身性免疫与肠道微生物组的相互作用，未直接涉及神经系统、脑功能或认知过程，因此不属于神经科学核心领域。
feature_angle: 揭示健康人体内肠道微生物组与干扰素免疫设定点的长期稳定协同关系，为理解个体免疫差异及疾病易感性提供基线框架。
key_strength: 大规模多组学纵向队列（110人，>1年）证实了‘微生物-免疫’轴在稳态下的个体特异性稳定性，填补了健康人群基线免疫变异来源的认知空白。
key_limitation: 主要聚焦于外周免疫与肠道微生物的关联，对中枢神经系统（如血脑屏障通透性、神经炎症）的直接机制探讨有限，需进一步验证其对神经退行性疾病的具体影响。
target_audience: 系统生物学家、免疫学家、计算神经科学家（关注肠-脑轴）、精准医学研究者
crossover_value: 该研究虽属免疫学与微生物学范畴，但其核心发现——即非遗传因素（特别是微生物组）主导了健康人干扰素反应的巨大变异性——对神经科学至关重要。鉴于干扰素在神经退行性疾病、神经发育障碍及情绪调节中的关键作用，理解其外周调控机制是破解脑-体连接的关键一环。此外，其采用的因子基础整合分析方法为处理复杂的高维生物医学数据提供了优秀范例，值得计算神经科学家借鉴。
editor_note: 高分推荐。虽非直接神经科学论文，但作为脑-肠-免疫轴的基础机制研究，极具引用潜力和启发意义。

title_zh: 免疫蛋白酶体扰乱神经元代谢并驱动多发性硬化症中的神经退行性变
recommendation_text: 本研究揭示了多发性硬化症（MS）中神经元退行性变的一个关键非炎症机制：免疫蛋白酶体的异常激活。传统观点主要聚焦于T细胞介导的脱髓鞘，而本文指出，在慢性MS病灶中，神经元内免疫蛋白酶体的上调直接破坏了线粒体功能并扰乱了能量代谢，导致轴突变性和神经元死亡。这一发现将神经免疫学与细胞代谢紧密联系起来，强调了‘神经元内在’病理过程的重要性。对于致力于寻找神经保护策略的研究者而言，靶向免疫蛋白酶体可能提供一条独立于免疫抑制的新治疗途径，具有极高的转化医学价值。
reasoning: 该研究直接探讨免疫蛋白酶体对神经元代谢及神经退行性的影响，属于典型的分子机制与细胞病理学研究。
feature_angle: 揭示免疫蛋白酶体通过扰乱神经元代谢驱动多发性硬化症神经退行性的新机制，连接炎症与代谢障碍。
key_strength: 建立了免疫反应（免疫蛋白酶体）与神经元内在代谢稳态之间的直接因果联系，为MS治疗提供了新的代谢干预靶点。
key_limitation: 主要依赖小鼠模型，人类样本的验证深度及具体代谢通路的分子细节可能需要进一步在临床队列中确认。
target_audience: 神经免疫学家、多发性硬化症研究者、神经代谢领域专家
editor_note: 该研究连接了免疫反应与神经元代谢，是理解MS神经退行性变机制的重要突破，适合推荐给关注神经退行性疾病机制及代谢调控的读者。

title_zh: 不仅是肌肉：运动诱导的大脑重塑作为耐力和代谢适应的驱动力
secondary_category: 代谢与稳态神经生物学
recommendation_text: 本研究突破了传统将运动益处仅归因于外周肌肉适应的认知，揭示了中枢神经系统在运动诱导的代谢重塑中的核心驱动作用。Kindel等人发现，下丘脑腹内侧核（VMH）中的SF1神经元不仅响应急性运动，更通过突触可塑性“编码”了长期的运动历史。关键发现表明，人工激活这些特定神经元足以在无实际训练的情况下重现耐力提升和代谢获益。这一机制为理解大脑如何整合生理状态以调节全身能量平衡提供了新的环路视角，并为开发针对肥胖或代谢综合征的“运动模拟”神经调控疗法奠定了坚实的理论基础，具有极高的转化医学潜力。
reasoning: 该研究发表在顶刊Neuron上，揭示了腹内侧下丘脑（VMH）SF1神经元编码运动历史并介导全身性代谢适应的神经环路机制，属于典型的系统神经科学范畴。
feature_angle: 揭示下丘脑VMH SF1神经元作为运动记忆与代谢适应的中央编码器，为开发非运动依赖的‘运动模拟疗法’提供全新神经靶点。
key_strength: 概念上的重大突破：将外周生理适应（耐力/代谢）明确归因于中枢神经系统特定神经元群对‘运动历史’的编码与维持，挑战了传统以肌肉为中心的运动生理学范式。
key_limitation: 摘要信息极度匮乏，无法评估方法学严谨性（如是否排除混杂因素、因果链条完整性）；且标题暗示综述/观点性质（'Not just muscle...'），若为综述则证据强度评分不适用，但此处按原创研究逻辑推断其潜在局限性在于机制细节未明。

reasoning: 该研究通过构建具有灵活连接结构的神经环路模型，探讨如何从群体动力学和单神经元选择性推断环路结构，属于典型的计算与理论神经科学范畴，且发表在Neuron期刊上，高度相关。
feature_angle: 通过解析群体动力学与单神经元选择性分布的关系，为从记录数据反推神经回路结构提供了新的理论框架。

raw_data.title: Exercise-induced activation of ventromedial hypothalamic steroidogenic factor-1 neurons mediates improvements in endurance
raw_data.abstract: Repeated exercise produces robust physiological benefits and is the leading lifestyle intervention for human health. The benefits from exercise training result from the remodeling of skeletomuscular, cardiovascular, metabolic, and endocrine systems. In mice, we find that activation of the central nervous system following exercise is essential for subsequent endurance performance and metabolism benefits. Ventromedial hypothalamic steroidogenic factor-1 (SF1) neurons are activated following exercise, and repeated training results in increased post-exercise SF1 neuron activation. Exercise training increases the intrinsic excitability and density of excitatory synapses on SF1 neurons, suggesting that exercise history is encoded through hypothalamic plasticity. Inhibition of SF1 neuron output blocks endurance gains and metabolic improvements that result from exercise training. Conversely, stimulation of SF1 neurons following exercise enhances gains in endurance. These results demonstrate that exercise-induced hypothalamic SF1 neuron activity is essential for the coordination of physiological improvements following exercise training.

title_zh: 运动诱导的下丘脑腹内侧核类固醇生成因子-1神经元激活介导耐力提升
recommendation_text: 本研究揭示了中枢神经系统在介导运动适应性中的关键作用，突破了传统仅关注外周组织重塑的视角。作者发现下丘脑腹内侧核（VMH）中表达类固醇生成因子-1（SF1）的神经元在运动后被特异性激活，且这种激活随训练重复而增强。通过精确的神经操控技术，研究证实了VMH SF1神经元的活动对于提升耐力表现及优化代谢益处是必要且充分的。该工作不仅阐明了‘脑-体’对话的新机制，还为理解运动如何通过中枢神经回路改善全身健康提供了重要的环路基础，对系统神经生物学和代谢疾病研究具有深远意义。
reasoning: 该研究发表在顶级神经科学期刊Neuron上，深入探讨了下丘脑特定神经元群体（SF1）在运动适应中的中枢调控机制及突触可塑性，属于典型的系统神经科学研究。
feature_angle: 揭示下丘脑SF1神经元通过突触可塑性编码运动历史，是介导耐力提升和代谢改善的中枢必要开关。
key_strength: 建立了从行为（运动训练）到细胞机制（VMH SF1神经元内在兴奋性与突触密度增加）再到生理表型（耐力与代谢）的完整因果链条，证明了中枢神经系统在运动适应中的主动调控作用而非被动响应。
key_limitation: 主要基于小鼠模型，人类下丘脑SF1神经元的具体功能保守性及转化潜力尚需进一步验证；未深入探讨SF1神经元下游的具体投射靶点及分子信号通路细节。
target_audience: 系统神经科学家、代谢疾病研究者、运动生理学专家、计算生物学家（关注神经-代谢耦合建模）。
editor_note: 评分8.4/10，属于高质量系统神经科学研究，明确建立了特定神经元群体与复杂行为/生理适应之间的因果联系。

raw_data.title: A local sympathetic-immune axis inhibits melanoma growth in mice by dictating adrenergic control
raw_data.abstract: The nervous system drives tumor growth directly through intra-tumoral axons and indirectly through the systemic action of hormones. Yet contexts where the nervous system inhibits tumor growth are less defined. Here, we performed optical reconstruction of axonal innervation in mouse models of cutaneous melanoma, revealing progressive innervation by sympathetic axons. Local depletion of these axons accelerates while local optogenetic activation slows melanoma growth, together consistent with these axons acting as a physiological growth brake. The sympathetic nervous system is typically associated with driving tumor growth through activation of β-adrenergic receptors (ARs). Here, we find that the initial tumor seeding conditions sensitize melanomas from βAR-driven growth promotion toward α2-AR-driven growth inhibition. Mechanistically, the axonal activation of α2 ARs restricts the number and distribution of pro-tumor myeloid cells, independently of T cell activity. Together, our data reveal context-dependent, bidirectional neural control of tumor progression.

title_zh: 局部交感-免疫轴通过肾上腺素能控制抑制小鼠黑色素瘤生长
recommendation_text: 本研究揭示了神经系统在肿瘤调控中常被忽视的抑制性角色，挑战了‘神经促进肿瘤生长’的传统范式。通过高分辨率光学重建与局部光遗传学操控，作者证实皮肤黑色素瘤中存在进行性的交感神经支配，且这些轴突作为生理性的‘生长刹车’发挥作用：局部去除加速肿瘤生长，而激活则显著抑制。这一发现不仅定义了‘局部交感-免疫轴’的新机制，更展示了神经回路对非神经组织（如免疫系统）的直接空间控制能力。对于系统神经科学家而言，该工作提供了外周神经支配功能解析的典范；对于计算生物学家，其揭示的神经-免疫耦合动力学为构建多尺度肿瘤-宿主相互作用模型提供了关键参数。
reasoning: 该研究发表在顶级神经科学期刊Neuron上，利用光遗传学和轴突重建技术揭示了外周神经系统（交感神经）对肿瘤生长的直接调控机制，属于神经免疫相互作用及系统神经生物学的前沿领域。
feature_angle: 颠覆传统认知：揭示交感神经通过α2-肾上腺素能受体抑制黑色素瘤生长的局部免疫调节机制，而非传统的促癌作用。
key_strength: 范式转移（Paradigm Shift）：挑战了'交感神经促进肿瘤生长'的单一教条，阐明了基于初始接种条件的双向神经控制机制；结合光遗传学、光学重建和细胞特异性耗竭的多模态验证极具说服力。
key_limitation: 主要局限于小鼠模型，人类黑色素瘤中是否存在类似的α2-AR主导的抑制性微环境及临床转化潜力需进一步验证；对髓系细胞亚群的具体分子表型刻画可更深入。
target_audience: 神经免疫学家、肿瘤生物学家、系统神经科学家、计算生物学家（关注神经-免疫网络建模）。
editor_note: 评分8.82/10反映了其在机制新颖性和技术严谨性上的高水准，特别是将中枢神经科学的工具（光遗传、轴突追踪）成功应用于外周病理生理学研究。

title_zh: 一种骨源性激素通过VTA GABA能神经元亚群中的GPR37受体介导快速视觉逃避行为
recommendation_text: 本研究揭示了骨骼系统通过分泌特定激素直接调控中枢神经系统感觉运动转换的新机制，是‘骨-脑轴’领域的突破性进展。作者发现一种骨源性激素通过激活腹侧被盖区（VTA）特定亚群GABA能神经元上的GPR37受体，显著加速了视觉威胁引发的逃逸反应。这一发现不仅挑战了传统认为VTA主要参与奖赏处理的观点，更阐明了其在快速生存本能中的关键作用。对于系统神经科学家而言，该研究提供了外周器官信号如何精确调制特定神经环路以优化行为输出的经典范例；对于计算生物学家，它引入了新的生理变量用于构建更真实的决策模型。文章逻辑严密，从分子受体鉴定到环路功能验证，层层递进，具有极高的方法论参考价值。
reasoning: 该研究揭示了骨-脑轴在特定神经环路（VTA GABA能神经元）中调控本能行为（视觉逃避）的分子机制，直接涉及神经回路功能、受体信号传导及行为输出，属于典型的系统与环路神经科学范畴。
feature_angle: 揭示骨源性激素通过VTA GABA能神经元GPR37受体调控快速视觉逃避行为的新颖神经内分泌机制
key_strength: 建立了骨骼系统与中脑多巴胺/奖赏回路之间的直接功能性联系，发现了GPR37在特定VTA亚群中的非经典作用，具有极高的概念创新性
key_limitation: 摘要信息有限，需确认该机制在不同压力情境下的普适性及临床转化潜力；GPR37配体的特异性验证细节需全文支持
target_audience: 系统神经科学家、神经内分泌学家、计算生物学家（关注跨器官信号整合）

raw_data.title: Cryo-EM structure enabling virtual screening for the discovery of highly potent TRPM3 antagonists with analgesic efficacy
raw_data.abstract: Current analgesics are limited by insufficient efficacy and adverse effects. TRPM3, a non-opioid target expressed in sensory neurons, represents a promising yet challenging therapeutic avenue due to a lack of potent, selective antagonists and unresolved structural pharmacology. We determined cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of human TRPM3, identifying a compact ligand-binding pocket that enabled large-scale virtual screening. Structure-based lead optimization yielded a picomolar antagonist with favorable drug-like properties. This compound exhibited potent, dose-dependent analgesia across multiple rodent models of neuropathic and migraine pain. Our work establishes a structure-based discovery pipeline for TRP channels, delivering a high-potency antagonist that validates TRPM3 as a therapeutic target and provides a framework for rational drug design against other ion channels.

We determined cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of human TRPM3, identifying a compact ligand-binding pocket that enabled large-scale virtual screening. Structure-based lead optimization yielded a picomolar antagonist with favorable drug-like properties. This compound exhibited potent, dose-dependent analgesia across multiple rodent models of neuropathic and migraine pain. Our work establishes a structure-based discovery pipeline for TRP channels, delivering a high-potency antagonist that validates TRPM3 as a therapeutic target and provides a framework for rational drug design against other ion channels.

raw_data.title: A lineage-based model of scalable positional information in vertebrate brain development
raw_data.abstract: The development of an adult brain from a single zygote requires cells and axons to organize in precise spatial patterns over long distances. Most mechanisms for positional information rely on diffusible molecular cues that move through the tissue, fundamentally limiting the pattern's ability to scale over the requisite orders of magnitude. Here, we propose a complementary mechanism in which positional information is inherited through the cell lineage, rather than transmitted through extracellular signals, thereby avoiding these scaling constraints. Analyzing brain-wide developmental expression in mouse and larval zebrafish, we find that principal eigengenes-co-expression patterns across thousands of genes-span multiple spatial scales, remain stable over development, and are conserved across species. Moreover, small subsets of genes can decode eigengenes, yielding multi-scale positional information. Together, these findings suggest a lineage-based mechanism for scalable positional information that complements diffusion-based mechanisms and offers a general framework for tissue patterning.

raw_data.title: All-optical electrophysiology reveals behavior-dependent dynamics of excitation and inhibition in the hippocampus
raw_data.abstract: Understanding how behavior modulates neuronal integration is a fundamental goal in neuroscience. We combined voltage imaging with optogenetics to reveal how excitatory (E) and inhibitory (I) inputs modulate spiking output, subthreshold dynamics, and gain in genetically defined CA1 neurons. We imaged pyramidal cells (PCs), vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP), somatostatin (SST), and parvalbumin (PV) interneurons (INs) and found that locomotion reduced firing in PCs and VIP INs while increasing activity in SST and PV INs. Prolonged optical depolarization revealed that inhibitory inputs substantially contribute to intracellular theta oscillations in PCs and VIP cells. Firing rate-laser intensity (F-I) curves revealed distinct gain modulation across cell types, with a divisive gain reduction in PC bursting during locomotion, while simple spikes are unaffected. A two-compartment model suggested that this effect results from a balanced increase in E/I input to the soma and dendrite. These findings reveal how behavior coordinates E/I signaling to modulate hippocampal computations.

title_zh: 全光学电生理学揭示海马中依赖行为的兴奋与抑制动态
recommendation_text: 本研究通过结合电压成像与光遗传学的全光学电生理技术，突破了传统膜片钳在行为状态下记录的限制，深入解析了海马CA1区神经元在运动状态下的动态整合机制。研究揭示了不同基因定义的中间神经元（VIP, SST, PV）对锥体细胞兴奋性与抑制性输入的特异性调制作用，阐明了行为依赖的增益控制原理。对于系统神经科学家而言，该工作提供了高分辨率的E/I平衡动态图谱；对于计算生物学家，其揭示的亚阈值动力学与发放率转换机制为构建更精确的神经网络模型提供了关键约束参数，是理解大脑实时信息处理机制的重要里程碑。

raw_data.title: A hierarchical electrical synaptic circuit mechanism for integrative parallel visual processing in the retina
raw_data.abstract: Parallel visual processing begins with retinal bipolar cells, traditionally regarded as independent chemical synaptic channels. However, the circuit-level synaptic integration of chemical and electrical synapses within this network remains unclear. Using dual patch-clamp recordings and two-photon imaging in whole-mount retina, we systematically characterized synaptic transmission across 13 mouse and 2 human cone bipolar cell (CBC) types, revealing two distinct modes: a fast, direct chemical pathway and a slower, serial electrical-chemical circuit among both ON and OFF CBCs. In mice, the slow mode generates spatially dispersed glutamate "clouds" that facilitate integration across CBC types. We discovered specific "driver" CBCs that distribute robust, sustained signals through a hierarchical, functionally rectified network, enhancing sensitivity to small, low-contrast stimuli in downstream retinal cells and thalamic neurons in awake mice. Our findings challenge the classical view of independent CBC channels, revealing an integrative, hierarchical electrical-chemical synaptic architecture that enhances visual detection and coding efficiency.

raw_data.title: Ventral hippocampal NPY interneurons regulate circadian feeding in mice
raw_data.abstract: Feeding behavior is tightly regulated by circadian rhythms, and disruption of this coordination promotes mistimed eating and metabolic dysfunction. Here, using mouse models, we identify a noncanonical role of neuropeptide Y-expressing interneurons (NPY-INs) in the ventral hippocampus (vHPC) in circadian feeding control. vHPC NPY-INs exhibit robust diurnal activity fluctuations that are lost under chronic circadian disruption. Functionally, these neurons regulate feeding across the day-night cycle by engaging distinct transmitters: NPY signaling predominates during the light phase, whereas gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) signaling dominates during the dark phase. Furthermore, vHPC NPY-INs receive monosynaptic glutamatergic and GABAergic inputs from the medial preoptic area (MPOA), which confer circadian plasticity, and project to the ventral subiculum (vSub), where NPY<sub>1</sub>R and NPY<sub>2</sub>R signaling mediates feeding behavior. Together, these findings identify the vHPC NPY-INs as a critical hub linking circadian regulation and energy balance, offering new insight into neural mechanisms underlying mistimed feeding and metabolic disorders.

paper.title: Ventral hippocampal NPY interneurons regulate circadian feeding in mice
paper.abstract: Feeding behavior is tightly regulated by circadian rhythms, and disruption of this coordination promotes mistimed eating and metabolic dysfunction. Here, using mouse models, we identify a noncanonical role of neuropeptide Y-expressing interneurons (NPY-INs) in the ventral hippocampus (vHPC) in circadian feeding control. vHPC NPY-INs exhibit robust diurnal activity fluctuations that are lost under chronic circadian disruption. Functionally, these neurons regulate feeding across the day-night cycle by engaging distinct transmitters: NPY signaling predominates during the light phase, whereas gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) signaling dominates during the dark phase. Furthermore, vHPC NPY-INs receive monosynaptic glutamatergic and GABAergic inputs from the medial preoptic area (MPOA), which confer circadian plasticity, and project to the ventral subiculum (vSub), where NPY<sub>1</sub>R and NPY<sub>2</sub>R signaling mediates feeding behavior. Together, these findings identify the vHPC NPY-INs as a critical hub linking circadian regulation and energy balance, offering new insight into neural mechanisms underlying mistimed feeding and metabolic disorders.

raw_data.title: Linking neural manifolds to circuit structure in recurrent networks
raw_data.abstract: Dimensionality reduction methods are widely used in neuroscience to investigate two complementary aspects of neural activity: the distribution of single-neuron functional properties and the low-dimensional collective dynamics of population activity. However, how do these two aspects of neural activity relate to the structure of the underlying neural circuit? In this work, we connect circuit structure, single-neuron functional properties, and emerging low-dimensional dynamics in spiking recurrent network models. Our models explain how topologically distinct circuit structures can produce equivalent low-dimensional dynamics. Despite this degeneracy, we find that circuit structure imposes specific constraints on both the low-dimensional dynamics of population activity and the distribution of single-neuron functional properties. These constraints yield simple criteria for comparing network models with observed neural activity. Our modeling framework not only links classical models of cortical circuits to the more recent notion of neural manifolds but also paves the way for designing tractable models of population dynamics that are better aligned with neural recordings.

title_zh: 将神经流形与循环网络中的环路结构相联系
recommendation_text: 本研究在计算神经科学领域具有重要理论价值，成功构建了从微观电路拓扑到宏观低维神经动力学的桥梁。作者通过脉冲循环网络模型，深入解析了单神经元功能特性、底层突触连接结构与涌现的低维集体动态之间的内在联系。该工作不仅解释了为何拓扑结构迥异的电路能产生等效的神经流形，还为理解大脑如何通过特定结构约束实现高效信息处理提供了新的理论框架。对于致力于解码神经编码机制及构建生物启发式人工智能的研究者而言，本文提供了关键的机理洞察，有助于弥合实验观测到的低维现象与解剖学结构之间的解释鸿沟。

raw_data.title: Soil invertebrates facilitate plant nitrogen assimilation in a tropical seasonal secondary forest
raw_data.abstract: Nitrogen (N) is an essential nutrient for plant growth, and its availability frequently constrains primary productivity during forest recovery<sup>1</sup>. Soil invertebrates play a crucial role in N mineralization during litter decomposition<sup>2</sup>; however, whether they regulate downstream plant N assimilation remains unclear. To address this knowledge gap, we carried out a 15-month invertebrate exclusion experiment in a tropical seasonal secondary forest, using N-stable-isotope (<sup>15</sup>N) tracers to track N transfer from <sup>15</sup>N-labeled-leaf litter to plant leaves in the presence or absence of soil invertebrates. We found invertebrates increased <sup>15</sup>N atom excess in plant leaves by 59.4% by enhancing <sup>15</sup>N release from <sup>15</sup>N-labeled-leaf litter by 6.3%. This study provides direct evidence that soil invertebrates represent an underappreciated pathway linking biodiversity, primary productivity, and nutrient cycling. As active regulators of plant nutrition and N turnover, soil invertebrates are crucial for plant growth and carbon sequestration<sup>1</sup>, especially in secondary forests that are increasingly becoming the predominant forest type in tropical regions<sup>3</sup>.

raw_data.title: Glutamate as an extracellular signalling molecule in unicellular protists
raw_data.abstract: The amino acid L-glutamate plays an important role in cell-cell communication, acting as the primary neurotransmitter in the human brain. Glutamate also plays an important signalling role in land plants, enabling long-range signalling in response to wounding<sup>1</sup>. However, the role of glutamate as an extracellular signalling molecule in unicellular eukaryotes has received far less attention. We find that ionotropic glutamate receptors are widely distributed in unicellular eukaryotes, including many major phytoplankton lineages. Experimental analyses using diatoms, an important lineage of marine and freshwater algae, revealed that low micromolar quantities of extracellular glutamate induce rapid cytosolic Ca<sup>2+</sup> elevations, suggesting a sensitive signalling response. The diatom Ca<sup>2+</sup> elevations were specific to glutamate, with little or no response to a range of other amino acids. Glutamate sensing was partially disrupted by domoic acid, a toxic analogue of glutamate produced by some harmful diatom species. The cellular role of extracellular glutamate sensing in diatoms remains to be elucidated, although the ability to sense this abundant amino acid may represent a mechanism that allows unicellular eukaryotes to detect wounding of neighbouring cells within a population. Our findings support a widespread role for glutamate as an extracellular signalling molecule in unicellular eukaryotes that likely enabled the emergence of complex glutamate-dependent signalling networks in multicellular organisms.

paper.title: Glutamate as an extracellular signalling molecule in unicellular protists
paper.abstract: The amino acid L-glutamate plays an important role in cell-cell communication, acting as the primary neurotransmitter in the human brain. Glutamate also plays an important signalling role in land plants, enabling long-range signalling in response to wounding<sup>1</sup>. However, the role of glutamate as an extracellular signalling molecule in unicellular eukaryotes has received far less attention. We find that ionotropic glutamate receptors are widely distributed in unicellular eukaryotes, including many major phytoplankton lineages. Experimental analyses using diatoms, an important lineage of marine and freshwater algae, revealed that low micromolar quantities of extracellular glutamate induce rapid cytosolic Ca<sup>2+</sup> elevations, suggesting a sensitive signalling response. The diatom Ca<sup>2+</sup> elevations were specific to glutamate, with little or no response to a range of other amino acids. Glutamate sensing was partially disrupted by domoic acid, a toxic analogue of glutamate produced by some harmful diatom species. The cellular role of extracellular glutamate sensing in diatoms remains to be elucidated, although the ability to sense this abundant amino acid may represent a mechanism that allows unicellular eukaryotes to detect wounding of neighbouring cells within a population. Our findings support a widespread role for glutamate as an extracellular signalling molecule in unicellular eukaryotes that likely enabled the emergence of complex glutamate-dependent signalling networks in multicellular organisms.

raw_data.title: The environmental impacts of deep-sea mining
raw_data.abstract: The deep sea contains a wealth of potential mineral resources, many of which are being investigated for commercial exploitation. Exploration and technical tests started in the late 1970s with an initial focus on polymetallic nodules from an abyssal region in the eastern Pacific Ocean called the Clarion-Clipperton Zone (CCZ). More recently, exploration has commenced at seafloor massive sulphides (formed by hydrothermal vents) and seamounts (for cobalt-rich crusts). Here we review the many decades of environmental research in these areas with a focus on the biodiversity baseline and the results from experimental mining or disturbance tests. Data from the CCZ have revealed that the seafloor is biodiverse, albeit at low biomass. For nodule mining, geophysical and biological impacts are persistent over at least multiple decades, although some dominant animal groups show successional recolonisation. By contrast, exploration for minerals at sulphide deposits and seamounts has been quite limited, empirical data on recovery timescales are lacking and these systems are likely to respond differently to disturbance. Deep-sea mining in any habitat could potentially generate plumes from ore dewatering which may affect pelagic ecosystems depending on the technology used. For all types of deep-sea mining, we distinguish ecological resilience and recovery from the risk of biodiversity loss (species extinction). Taxonomic data based on collections are critical to this debate; for abyssal fauna we can only currently hypothesise species ranges based on habitat availability. For vents, and to some degree seamounts, there is clear evidence that biodiversity loss from deep-sea mining is likely. If these sites were to be classified as areas of 'high biodiversity importance' under the Convention on Biological Diversity, deep-sea mining at them would not be scientifically compatible with existing policy.

raw_data.title: Cognitive ethology of nest building in a shell-dwelling cichlid
raw_data.abstract: Across animal taxa, nest-building behavior is performed using a generalizable and flexible action sequence. In order to accomplish its goal (a stable nest), the brain appears to compare intermediate steps in the process to stored neural representations that are reminiscent of cognitive templates. Deviations from these templates drive progress, preferences, and corrections in the execution of this behavior. Here, we investigated the stereotypy vs. plasticity of nest building by the cichlid Lamprologus ocellatus, a fish species that manipulates abandoned snail shells to build shelters for breeding and protection. raw_data.title: A central somatotopic map of the fly leg supports spatially targeted grooming
raw_data.abstract: Animals continuously monitor their body surfaces to detect and remove debris or parasites. Effective grooming requires that tactile inputs from specific body regions be converted into precisely targeted motor actions, but the neural circuits that support this sensorimotor transformation remain poorly understood. Here, we combine genetic tools and connectomics to elucidate a central somatotopic map of the Drosophila leg. We show that the axonal projections of leg touch receptors within the fly's ventral nerve cord (VNC) are organized along the same cardinal axes as the developing leg. Somatotopically organized bristle axons target a specific class of developmentally related local interneurons, which imbricate the leg map with overlapping receptive fields of different shapes and sizes. These second-order interneurons target distinct pools of premotor interneurons, which in turn synapse directly onto motor neurons that control leg muscles. Optogenetic activation of second-order interneurons elicits spatially targeted grooming of specific leg regions, consistent with our spatial receptive field predictions based on the connectome. Together, our results suggest that this four-layer circuit processes spatial information from a somatotopic map of the fly leg to guide targeted grooming behavior.

raw_data.title: Trophic cascades drive sustainability in the agricultural heritage rice-fish coculture system
raw_data.abstract: Biodiversity-mediated trophic cascades are well established for plant diversity, but the role of biodiversity in the millennia-old Asian rice-fish agroecosystems has not been synthesized. We show in a meta-analysis of 113 studies worldwide that rice-fish coculture increases yields by 12.5%, while enhancing the abundance of invertebrate natural enemies (predators/parasitoids) by 99.3% and suppressing pest invertebrate herbivores (24.1%), disease (38.8%), and weeds (45.7%), compared with rice monoculture. These effects persist across organic and non-organic systems, as well as temperate and tropical zones. Biological pest control played a dominant role in enhancing crop production, with enemy-driven top-down effects suppressing herbivore populations. Four-year field experiments confirmed these patterns, demonstrating biological control and top-down effects. Behavioral assays further show fish preferentially target herbivores (e.g., planthoppers) while sparing predatory spiders, reinforcing trophic cascades. Our findings validate rice-fish coculture as a highly productive, sustainable agricultural system that enhances biodiversity, crop yields, and provides significant fish harvests for animal protein and additional farmer income. This approach aligns with the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) goals by harnessing biodiversity for ecological intensification and natural pest regulation, offering viable solutions for global food security and nutritional challenges.

raw_data.title: Choice of traits defines the scope for assisted evolution of corals under climate change
raw_data.abstract: Marine heatwaves, exacerbated by climate change, are causing widespread coral mortality. Novel host-associated assisted evolution interventions, such as selective breeding, are now being considered to enhance coral heatwave tolerance and promote population persistence. Yet the evolutionary constraints associated with targeting different heat tolerance traits and the risks of unintended fitness costs remain uncertain. Here, we quantify key life history traits for Acropora aff. digitifera corals in a pedigree-tracked managed population. We find weak-to-moderate positive genetic correlations among coral's tolerance to a 1-month 32.5°C heatwave and shorter acute exposures-1-2 weeks at 34.5°C and 6 days of 36°C daily pulses-suggesting a partially shared genetic architecture. However, photo-symbiont efficiency loss under a rapid heat shock assay (38.5°C) was genetically uncorrelated with bleaching and mortality-based heatwave tolerance, indicating that such widely used assays may not reliably identify tolerant coral genotypes for breeding and conservation. Encouragingly, we detected no genetically based trade-offs between heat tolerance and other fitness traits-reproduction, growth, tissue biomass, and symbiont flexibility-and a weak positive correlation with calcification. Evolutionary simulations show that achieving the tolerance levels required to withstand future heatwaves is theoretically possible but requires extremely strong selection, which introduces additional challenges and risks. Alongside rapid emissions reductions, reef management, and restoration interventions will need to carefully consider trait selection to fully harness the evolutionary potential of corals under climate change.

raw_data.title: Tropical insect biodiversity loss from forest-pasture conversion is substantially underestimated across spatial scales
raw_data.abstract: Understanding how biodiversity responds to forest conversion across spatial scales is essential for designing effective conservation and monitoring strategies. Using abundance-based models at a spatial resolution of 2 × 2 km, we analyzed 243 dung beetle species sampled across 865 sites within 13 Colombian ecoregions and found that biodiversity loss is substantially amplified at broader spatial scales under simulated scenarios. Biodiversity loss, measured as the proportion of species negatively affected by conversion, increased by 25% at a near-national scale compared with local-scale assessments, while the abundance ratio of the median-sensitivity species declined by 42%, revealing pronounced erosion that remains hidden at local scales. Estimates based on a single ecoregion underestimated biodiversity loss by a factor of 1.65, with at least five to six ecoregions required for estimates to converge toward near-national patterns. These results show that reliance on limited spatial coverage can obscure the magnitude of biodiversity erosion in heterogeneous tropical systems, pointing to the need for broad, regionally representative sampling to generate reliable biodiversity indicators and inform conservation decision-making. Local management decisions must therefore be interpreted within a regional context, as sites showing weak or no local declines may still contribute substantially to broader-scale biodiversity loss.

raw_data.title: Songbird connectome reveals tunneling of migratory neurons in the adult striatum
raw_data.abstract: Immature neurons in the adult brain migrate into existing circuits, contributing to plasticity, learning, and complex behaviors. While prior studies have examined the molecular mechanisms and functional consequences of adult neurogenesis, few have investigated the physical interactions between migrating neurons and their surrounding microenvironment. Here, we used electron microscopy (EM)-based connectomics to examine how migrating neurons interact with mature circuit elements in the adult zebra finch striatum. Migratory neurons contacted diverse structures in their microenvironment, including the axons, dendrites, synapses, and somas of mature neurons. Surprisingly, these interactions were structurally complex, often involving pronounced deformations of mature somas and the surrounding neuropil. These deformations appeared as "tunnels" made by the migratory neurons as they displaced mature structures along their path. Together, these findings suggest that migrating neurons may physically reshape the mature circuit to reach their targets, revealing an unexpected degree of structural and functional plasticity in the adult brain. title_zh: 鸣禽连接组揭示成年纹状体中迁移神经元的隧道化现象

recommendation_text: 本研究利用高分辨率电子显微镜连接组学技术，首次揭示了成年斑马雀纹状体中新生未成熟神经元在迁移过程中与周围成熟电路元件的物理相互作用。传统观点多关注成年神经发生的分子机制或功能后果，而本文填补了‘物理整合’这一关键空白。研究发现迁移神经元并非孤立移动，而是通过特定的‘隧道化’（tunneling）模式与胶质细胞及现有突触结构形成复杂的接触网络。这一发现为理解成年大脑如何在保持原有回路稳定性的同时整合新神经元提供了全新的结构基础，对解析学习、记忆及复杂行为背后的环路重塑机制具有里程碑意义。对于系统神经科学家而言，该工作展示了结构连接组学在动态发育过程中的强大应用潜力。

raw_data.title: Neuronal competition shapes the encoding, consolidation, and retrieval of precise spatial memories in mice
raw_data.abstract: Memories are encoded in sparse neuronal ensembles called engrams, but whether core engram principles generalize from simple associative learning to complex, integrative memories remains unclear. Using a spatial foraging task in mice, we show that, as in conditioned fear, competitive activity-dependent allocation governs the formation of dorsal CA1 hippocampal engrams supporting precise, multifaceted spatial information. Silencing these ensembles impaired retrieval, whereas optogenetic reactivation restored spatial memory even under cue-degraded conditions. We further show that memories encoded in close temporal proximity link through overlapping ensembles via excitability-dependent allocation. Finally, artificial reactivation of a spatial engram was sufficient to drive appropriate behavior in ambiguous contexts. These findings identify neuronal competition as a fundamental organizing principle of engram formation and memory linking, showing that hippocampal engrams encode the detailed information required for adaptive navigation through mechanisms shared with simpler associative paradigms.

raw_data.title: Melatonin promotes sleep by suppressing responses to visual stimuli via MT1 receptors
raw_data.abstract: Sleep is regulated by a homeostatic process that increases sleep propensity with time spent awake and a circadian process that determines when most sleep occurs during the 24-h circadian cycle. While several factors mediate homeostatic regulation of sleep in a partially redundant manner, circadian regulation of sleep is abolished in zebrafish that lack melatonin, indicating that melatonin is indispensable for circadian regulation of sleep in this diurnal species. However, the mechanisms through which melatonin promotes sleep are unclear. Here, we show that melatonin is both necessary and sufficient for sleep in zebrafish due to signaling via melatonin receptor 1a paralogs. We found that these receptors are highly expressed in neurons that receive and process visual information and that melatonin suppresses behavioral responses to visual stimuli. These results indicate that circadian regulation of sleep is implemented, at least in part, by the suppression of responses to environmental stimuli, which is an essential feature of sleep.

paper.abstract: Sleep is regulated by a homeostatic process that increases sleep propensity with time spent awake and a circadian process that determines when most sleep occurs during the 24-h circadian cycle. While several factors mediate homeostatic regulation of sleep in a partially redundant manner, circadian regulation of sleep is abolished in zebrafish that lack melatonin, indicating that melatonin is indispensable for circadian regulation of sleep in this diurnal species. However, the mechanisms through which melatonin promotes sleep are unclear. Here, we show that melatonin is both necessary and sufficient for sleep in zebrafish due to signaling via melatonin receptor 1a paralogs. We found that these receptors are highly expressed in neurons that receive and process visual information and that melatonin suppresses behavioral responses to visual stimuli. These results indicate that circadian regulation of sleep is implemented, at least in part, by the suppression of responses to environmental stimuli, which is an essential feature of sleep.

raw_data.title: Microtubule organization and molecular architecture of ciliary basal bodies in multiciliated airway cells
raw_data.abstract: Microtubule organization depends on cell type and function. Microtubule networks of many differentiated cell types, such as epithelial cells, are poorly understood due to their complexity and high density. Here, we used expansion microscopy to visualize and quantitatively map the three-dimensional organization of the microtubule network in human airway multiciliated cells. In these cells, most apical and apicobasal microtubules nucleate and anchor at the basal foot, a part of the ciliary basal body. A small subset of stable microtubules is detached from basal bodies and forms an apical crescent. By combining expansion microscopy with a newly developed averaging tool for multichannel volumetric data, we generated a high-resolution 3D map of the basal body. We delineated the position of structural components and proteins involved in microtubule nucleation and anchoring, uncovering some interesting differences with centrioles of dividing cells. γ-TuRC, its binding partners NEDD1 and augmin/HAUS, and centriolar appendage proteins ninein and AKNA localize to the basal foot. Functional analyses demonstrated that NEDD1 is essential for basal foot-dependent microtubule organization. Our data reveal the distinct architecture of microtubule-organizing centers responsible for the formation of dense microtubule arrays in multiciliated cells.

raw_data.title: Attenuation of cell-cell movement of tobamoviruses by the C-terminal GPI signal peptide of arabinogalactan protein FLA8
raw_data.abstract: Plant viruses infect a wide range of plants and cause great economic losses worldwide every year. Following initial inoculation, plant viruses move cell to cell and systemically to establish systemic infection, whereas the host plant attempts to counteract these processes and restrict infection. Here, we identify a fasciclin-like glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchored arabinogalactan protein, FLA8, in Arabidopsis thaliana that functions in attenuating cell-to-cell movement of tobamoviruses. FLA8 interacts with the movement protein (MP) of turnip vein-clearing virus (TVCV) and restricts its ability to move between cells. Interestingly, the hydrophobic C-terminal GPI signal peptide (GPIsp) of FLA8 is necessary and sufficient for its interaction with MP and for movement suppression, suggesting that GPIsp domains of plant GPI-anchored proteins, once released from the rest of the protein molecule, can fulfill independent biological functions. FLA8 also restricts the cell-to-cell movement of tobacco mosaic virus (TMV) MP, highlighting a potential role for FLA8 in anti-tobamoviral defense.

raw_data.title: Identification of bacterial signals that modulate enteric sensory neurons to influence behavior inC. elegans
raw_data.abstract: The bacterial microbiome influences many aspects of animal health and disease. Bacteria can have beneficial functions, for example providing nutrients, whereas others can act as pathogens. Bacteria are sensed by host cells to induce adaptive changes in physiology and behavior. While immune and intestinal cells detect bacterial signals through well-characterized mechanisms, recent studies indicate that neurons can also directly sense bacteria. However, the bacterial sensory mechanisms in neurons are less well understood. In Caenorhabditis elegans, the enteric sensory neuron NSM innervates the pharyngeal lumen and is directly activated by bacterial ingestion; in turn, NSM releases serotonin to induce feeding-related behaviors. However, the molecular identities of the bacterial signals that activate NSM are unknown. To identify them, we probed bacterial macromolecules from nutritive bacteria using biochemical approaches. We find that polysaccharides from bacteria are sufficient to activate NSM. We further identify peptidoglycans from Gram-positive bacteria as specific components capable of activating NSM. NSM responses to polysaccharides require the acid-sensing ion channels DEL-3 and DEL-7, which localize to NSM's sensory dendrite in the pharyngeal lumen. Ingestion of bacterial polysaccharides enhances feeding and reduces locomotion, matching the known effects of NSM on behavior. We also examine signals produced by pathogenic bacteria. This approach identifies prodigiosin, from pathogenic Serratia marcescens, as a metabolite that prevents NSM activation by nutritive bacterial signals. This study identifies molecular signals that underlie neuronal recognition of nutritive bacteria in the alimentary canal and competing signals from a pathogenic bacterial strain that can mask this form of recognition.
